sections.value:
READY / security PASS - round 2, final under C34

PR #246 at e56cb949d907dd41e9e77a52b64374f21928a851.
Reviewed the complete seven-file repair delta from
f3784caab656c1665c2daa469b283f60b2aa0065.
S246-001 and S246-002 are closed. No remaining blocking security finding
or new C34 follow-up is required by this review.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No remaining security vulnerabilities found | - |

S246-001 closed: the plan receipt uses repository-relative references at
docs/plans/231-spawn-cache-line/plan.dd.json:147 and its generated
plan.dd.md:171. The case-insensitive plan scan found no machine-home or
email match at this head. Earlier source-tree exposure is historical-only;
C19 requires the forward scrub, not a history rewrite.

S246-002 closed: crates/cli/src/main.rs:4643-4667 maps ordinary sidecar
failures to fixed identity-free descriptions AND replacement fixes.
The receipt uses these descriptions at :4605-4609. Transport error details
are removed at :4630-4633. Directory holder cache reasons now use the same
helper at :3644, so the adjacent human presentation does not retain the
old identity-bearing reason.

Displayed fields still pass through render::line. Core rendering,
spawn/revive dispatch, envelope serialization and JSON/success guards
are unchanged. No token, account identifier, local account path or upstream
credential is exposed by the repaired human presentations.

The new regression,
tests::the_receipt_line_never_shows_the_account_or_a_local_path
(crates/cli/src/main.rs:4937-5006), exercises account-bearing reasons AND
fixes, path-bearing reasons AND fixes, unknown states/reasons, and forged
multiline input. It asserts exact safe output and absence of the synthetic
identities and home paths. This directly covers the original privacy
failure instead of treating escaping as redaction.

Publication checks: the complete repair delta was inspected, including
the removed identifying text. Current PR title/body and both complete PR
commit messages contain no detected private identifier.
Case-insensitive git grep -n -i -I -E at the exact full head included
tracked hidden files. Full-tree matches relevant to the repair were
synthetic fixtures/assertions at main.rs:4963-5003 and policy prose at
plan.dd.json:149 / plan.dd.md:173, not private account data. Matched values
were captured and reduced to locations, never reproduced here.
The plan-only machine-home/email scan exited 1 with no matches.

Validation:
- just pr-freeze 246 --worktree: passed, FINAL at the requested full head;
  clean detached review worktree; both remote head probes agree; all five
  latest checks passed.
- gh run view 44430351257 --repo AI-Substrate/pij-fleet
  --json headSha,event,status,conclusion: succeeded and names the requested
  head; pull_request event.
- Rust-test job 135245837397 reported 2,509 passed and six skipped.
  Its successful upload log identifies artifact 14486377176. Reading that
  artifact by ID found 2,509 JUnit cases, zero failures/errors, and the new
  privacy regression passed. The six nextest skips are reported separately
  and are not represented as skipped cases in that JUnit XML.
- Rust lint, both Node jobs and delivers also passed.
- harness checks --quick in the exact-head detached review exited 1:
  pij-skill and copilot-native passed; dependency-dependent checks failed
  in the node_modules-less worktree; heavy route-inventory, Rust and smoke
  stages were skipped. No dependency symlink was created. This is not a
  full local harness pass or a full product-readiness certification.

Proof limits: source review and associated Linux CI, not a live fleet
spawn/revive exercise or an exact-head macOS Rust build. Product source and
tracked review-worktree files were not changed by this review.
Cost: no new recurring loop, timer, poll or process launch; the repair
changes request-driven in-process human formatting only.

Harness improvement: the new privacy regression now gives deterministic
backpressure against reintroducing account/path-bearing receipt text.
magicWand remains a dependency-free scoped review gate that separates
native-contract/CI receipts from full readiness and routes local Rust work
through the serialized nice-only build surface. The existing captured
dependency-free review difficulty is unchanged, not a new PR defect.
